newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Grains-Traders say US soybeans, soymeal sold.
newsitem.headline: China Grains-Traders say US soybeans, soymeal sold.

text.p: A panamax cargo of low protein U.S. soybean meal was heard committed to a buyer in the north China province of Shandong for forward delivery in August or September, grains sources said on Thursday.
"I think the deal was likely finalised (Wednesday) night," said one grains trader.
No price details were available.
A 50,000-tonne cargo of U.S. soybeans was heard sold for delivery in July to a south China port, but no price details were heard and the deal could not be confirmed.
"The buyers preferred the quality of U.S. beans, which is more consistent than that of beans from Brazil or Argentina," said a senior grains source.

Although Chinese buyers have largely shunned prompt shipments of soybeans and soybean meal despite the recent price drops on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), grains sources reported fresh Chinese enquiries in the forward months.
"The feed mills have stocks, but they are bullish for later on," said one China-based trader.
With both CBOT soybeans and soymeal in backwardation, where forward months were cheaper than spot contracts, China's buyers were looking to buy forward shipments, grains traders agreed.

South American soymeal for forward shipment in August or September was heard offered at below $320 per tonne, C&F China, while some traders pegged offers for South American meal for October or November delivery at $295 per tonne, C&F China.
"I've heard some deals were being negotiated (for November) but I'm not sure they were concluded," said one grains executive.
Demand for raw material in the feed industry was steady, traders and feed sources said.
The price of pork in China was holding steady at five yuan per "jin" (roughly equivalent to one pound) while chicken prices had dipped slightly to 3.5 yuan per jin, a feed executive said.
"Feed demand can only increase," he said.
Domestic soybean meal remained at 2,800 to 2,850 yuan per tonne, making any imports above $330 per tonne, C&F China, unprofitable, the executive said.
Domestic soybean prices also remained at 3,000 to 3,100 yuan per tonne, industry sources said.
China imported 253,000 tonnes of soybeans in March, down 93,000 tonnes from its February imports, the China Securities newspaper said earlier this month.
Total soybean imports for the first quarter of 1997 were 973,000 tonnes, close to the total imports for all of 1996.
March 1997 meal imports were 371,000 tonnes, 39,000 tonnes higher than the February meal imports.
First quarter soybean meal imports totalled 1.073 million tonnes, an increase of 483.1 percent over the same period in 1996.
The newspaper report said that the average price of imported soybeans CIF in March was US$294.60 per tonne.
